group.name: AgentFleet
group.description: Open-source monitoring and policy controls for coding-agent fleets

messages.text: One Rust binary per device. Collect coding-agent usage and tool events, send them to our server, and give the security team a web console. Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs for custom agents. Keep it open source.
The first vertical slice is in: sensor → POST /v1/events → Postgres → live console. Next is #184: make the outcome of a policy check honest.
For #184, show me what happens when an agent tries to read .env.production. Was it stopped, or did we only see it? Also, the file contents must never leave the device.
The Claude Code hook fixture stops the read. But the imported Codex observation gets the same green Blocked badge. That second event is only telemetry.
That is the bug. A deny decision is not proof the action was prevented. The event needs to say which actually happened.
Wren has the Rust change. Mara is on the console. Victor and the SDK owners are checking the same two event fixtures. Keep the pilot on hold until those agree.

group.name: Rust agent
group.description: crates/sensor · local checks, redacted events and the device queue

messages.text: The Linux service now resumes the disk queue after a restart. I still need to check what happens when the spool reaches its limit.
Found the bad assumption in the sensor serializer: `blocked = decision == Deny`. That is also used by the observation adapter, which has no way to stop the tool.
Pass the enforcement result in separately. Please leave Unknown as a real value; a missing result must not turn into Allowed.
Proposed fix attached. The serialized event keeps the tool name and resource class; the raw tool input is gone. The console and SDK changes are in the same diff.
Separate issue: a full spool currently drops the oldest audit event. That needs an explicit counter before we call the pilot ready.

group.name: Web console
group.description: web/ · device usage, policy matches and the live event timeline

messages.text: Device list is wired to the server. The usage chart is still counting sessions, not tokens; leaving the cost column out until the providers agree on units.
The event drawer is showing decision=deny and then deriving the Blocked badge from it. That is where the observation case goes wrong.
Changing the badge to use enforcement. The rule match stays in its own field. An observed attempt can still have matched a deny rule.
Can we avoid green for Blocked? Green reads like the command succeeded. I would use a neutral badge and put the policy match beside it.
Agreed. Also found that reconnect appends an event we already have. I will key rows by event_id, not their position in the stream.

group.name: Ingestion API
group.description: server/ · event validation, Postgres and the live stream

messages.text: Tenant ID comes from the device credential, never the event body. Event IDs are unique within a tenant.
Collector restart replays the last batch. Inserts deduplicate, but subscribers still get the duplicate notification. I opened #191 for that.
New contract: policy_decision is allow/deny; enforcement is enforced/observe_only/unknown. The server stores both. I am not inferring enforcement from the agent name.
The existing development events have no enforcement field. They will read as Unknown in the console. Reingesting them must not make them look blocked.
These are the two wire examples I am validating against. The only sensitive resource metadata is credential_file; no path or file contents.
Go SDK example is a tool callback around an agent runtime. No separate daemon required for that path; it sends the same event envelope as the sensor.
Python framework callback is observation-only today. Returning an audit event does not stop the framework from calling its tool.
The TypeScript wrapper copied the sensor's blocked flag. Fixing the envelope before I publish the next dev package.
Please make enforcement mandatory. Otherwise every SDK will eventually pick a different default.
Another bug: each retry creates a fresh event_id. That explains the duplicate rows Mara saw. I have a reproduction; fix is not in this diff yet.

group.name: Policy engine
group.description: policies/ · rule matches, local gates and coverage

messages.text: The credential-file rule evaluates on the device. A server round trip is not on the tool permission path.
The pilot case is a Claude Code Read hook. It does not demonstrate blocking arbitrary shell commands, child processes or every coding tool.
Right. The Codex path in this candidate imports observations. I am not adding a Blocked badge to those events.
For the audit payload: agent, tool name, policy ID, resource class, decision and enforcement. Raw arguments and environment values stay out.
Unknown is important when an adapter cannot confirm the result. Keep that distinct from both Observe only and Enforced.

group.name: Integration tests
group.description: fixtures/ · the same tool attempt from device to console

messages.text: Added a fake credential value to the test file. I am checking that it appears in neither the local queue nor the upload body.
Current failure: Codex observation with decision=deny renders Blocked. It should render Observed. Both cases are attached to #184.
The Python SDK fixture has the same problem. I will use the server's event pair rather than another handwritten example.
Linux job is through. macOS packaging is failing at signing, before the install test runs. That is still open; it is not an SDK test failure.

group.name: v0.3 pilot
group.description: Linux lab first · macOS package and SDK retries still open

messages.text: For the first pilot: a signed-in device sends an event, the console shows it, and the displayed outcome matches the adapter's actual capability.
macOS package is held by the signing job. The Linux artifact is available for the lab; nothing has been published.
Three open items: #184 outcome labels, #191 duplicate events, #193 spool-overflow counter. I am not bundling all of them into one PR.
Keep the first release small. One event I can follow through the code is better than a dashboard full of made-up numbers.
The proposed #184 diff is in Rust agent. It crosses the event schema, one Rust serializer, the console badge and the Python/TypeScript observation helpers. No policy changes.
The TypeScript retry issue needs a separate change. Are we happy to hold that package while the sensor work gets reviewed?
The current UI says Blocked for an event that never had a blocking integration. I would fix that before showing it to anyone outside the team.
AgentFleet is the working name. Repository is split into crates/sensor, server, web and sdks. I have kept the device protocol shared so each component does not invent its own event.

type.text: Keep #184 focused: show both events correctly, prove the audit payload contains no secret, and send me the diff. Leave the retry bug separate.

reply.text: Yes. Wren owns the envelope, Mara owns the display. Sonia, hold the TypeScript package until #191 is fixed.
The serializer now takes an enforcement result instead of guessing from deny. Observe-only events stay observe-only. I left the policy evaluator unchanged.
Validated the two fixtures. They both match the deny rule; only the hook case carries enforcement=enforced. Unknown is accepted and stays Unknown.
Both cases are visible now: Blocked for the enforced deny; Observed for the imported trace. The rule still reads credentials/no-read on both.
Python observation helper matches the schema. It sends metadata only and always marks its own output observe_only. A framework would need a separate gate to prevent execution.
TypeScript has the same change. The retry test still fails: two sends produce two IDs. Package stays on hold; I am fixing that on #191.

Replayed the two #184 fixtures through the candidate. Hook case: tool did not execute, console says Blocked. Imported observation: console says Observed. The canary credential value is absent from the queue and request body.
That covers the narrow Read-hook case. Keep the coverage note visible in the event detail; this is not evidence of general process-level prevention.
The outcome fix is ready to review. Still open: the TypeScript retry bug, spool-overflow reporting and macOS signing. Linux lab build only; no public release.
#184 is ready for your code review. The event path is consistent now. The wider pilot is still held on the three open items in v0.3 pilot.
Here is the review copy. The important change is that a rule decision and an enforcement result are separate fields. Please check the Unknown branch as well as the happy path.
